---
title: "METIS"
---

METIS learns a fast surrogate from a bank of simulator runs. Use it to make
predictions, generate new trajectories, or supply a learned density to a fitting
routine.

[Train your first surrogate](package/quickstart.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Install locally](basics/installing_metis.qmd){.btn .btn-secondary}

The tutorials show executed code, plots and results. Download a **Jupyter**
notebook or choose **Open in Colab** under **Other Formats** to run one yourself.
In Colab, choose **Runtime → Run all**; the first cell prepares the environment.

## Start with your simulations

1. [Work through a CSV example](package/own-bank.qmd) to load, train and save a model.
2. [Compare model families](package/model-choice.qmd) on held-out simulations.
3. [Check predictions and variability](package/evaluation.qmd) before using the surrogate.
4. [Reload it in your own application](package/deployment.qmd).

Use the Python API in notebooks and applications, or [Hydra](package/hydra.qmd)
for configuration files, experiment overrides and sweeps. Both use the same
training and evaluation code.

## Understand the models

METIS includes [MLPs](models/mlp.qmd) and [transformers](models/transformer.qmd)
for deterministic predictions, plus [flow matching](models/flow-matching.qmd)
and [normalising flows](models/normalising-flow.qmd) for stochastic trajectories.
Each model tutorial explains the idea and runs a small example.

For reference, see the [data format](package/data.qmd),
[API](package/api.qmd) and [troubleshooting](package/troubleshooting.qmd).
